topics: throughput/QPS and latency targets for reranking
hybrid search (BM25 + embeddings) and rerank cost
hosted vs dedicated vs private deployment tradeoffs
transcript:
[00:00] Jenna Park (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Jenna, AE on the account, and with me is Marco, our SE. How's everybody doing?
[00:12] Samir Patel (Nimbus): Good thanks, Jenna. Excited to dig in. We shipped the invite with a short agenda — embeddings, rerank flow, and questions around deployment modes — hosted vs dedicated vs private.
[00:30] Marco Diaz (Redwood SE): Great, quick intro on our side — Marco, I focus on performance and integrations. We'll try to cover architecture options and what a pilot would look like.
[00:42] Alyssa Chen (Nimbus): Awesome. Quick context: Nimbus runs a search product for financial docs. We currently use a hybrid approach — BM25 + vector-based rerank in a custom pipeline. We're evaluating options to standardize embeddings infra.
[01:10] Tom Ruiz (Nimbus SRE): Also we're sensitive to throughput — peak of around 800 QPS for search queries during market open, typical sustained 120 QPS. Latency SLO for search + rerank ideally sub-300ms 95th.
[01:35] Marco: Thanks, that's helpful. To confirm: the 800 QPS peak — is that queries that require full rerank for top 100 results, or sometimes just top 10?
[01:50] Samir: Good question — usually top 50 for rerank in prod, sometimes top 100 in experiments. We can tune.
[02:05] Jenna: Perfect. So there are a few axes — embedding model + dimensionality, vector DB choices and how we integrate (hosted Pinecone or self-hosted Milvus/OpenSearch), and whether Redwood hosts inference, you reserve Dedicated capacity, or Private in your VPC.
[02:20] Marco: One practical thing — if you want low-tail latency for rerank we typically suggest running the model close to the vector DB to avoid network hops, or use dedicated routing with caching for common prefixes. For Hosted we have regional endpoints and prefix caching, Dedicated gives you reserved GPU capacity, and Private gives you the ability to run within your VPC.
[03:05] Alyssa: How do you deal with dimensionality? Our current embeddings are 1536 dims from a custom fine-tuned model. Cost grows with dimension and so does vector DB storage.
[03:25] Marco: Right, dimensionality is a cost + latency factor. With 1536 you'll see larger tokenization and embedding compute. Redwood Optimize can suggest quantization and dimensionality tradeoffs — for example, 768 vs 1536 with a small eval set to see quality delta.
[04:00] Samir: We care about rerank accuracy; can't lose >2% MRR. So any dimensionality reduction needs to be validated.
[04:12] Marco: Absolutely — we run A/B evals tied to your prompt/queries. For rerank pipelines we also recommend a hybrid approach: vector search for recall, then a lightweight cross-encoder reranker for final scoring. That lets you keep candidate set small and reduce reranker QPS.
[04:45] Tom: What's the expected throughput for the reranker if we only rerank top 50?
[04:55] Marco: If you have 800 QPS and rerank top 50 per query, that's up to 40k rerank calls per second if each reranker call is per candidate — obviously you'd batch. In practice we batch across requests and use continuous batching to amortize cost. But you should dimension for peak concurrency.
[05:20] Samir: That 40k number is scary. Can you explain batching a bit more?
[05:30] Marco: Sure. Our runtime supports dynamic batching and kernel selection. If you can tolerate a few ms extra latency, the system aggregates multiple rerank requests into a single GPU batch. For example, batching 16 candidates at once reduces per-candidate latency and cost. This works best on Dedicated where you have predictable GPU pools, but Hosted can do it too with some variability.
[06:10] Jenna: Also worth noting prefix/KV caching for common queries reduces calls drastically for repeat traffic — we see large websites have heavy tail where top queries repeat a lot.
[06:28] Alyssa: On vector DB integration — does Redwood manage the index, or do we continue to host Pinecone/Milvus?
[06:40] Marco: Both patterns are supported. Many customers keep their vector DB (Pinecone/Milvus/OpenSearch) and call Redwood for inference only — we return embeddings or rerank scores. For tighter integration we provide connectors that can push embeddings into your DB, or we can host vector index in our Dedicated offering. For Private, everything runs in your VPC and you manage the DB there.
[07:10] Samir: If we go Hosted, how do you handle data residency and keys? We're under compliance constraints.
[07:20] Jenna: We have SOC 2, and for Hosted we offer region selection. For Dedicated we provide tenant isolation and dedicated GPU pools. For Private we can run the control plane with customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM) and full audit logs. We'll send the compliance packet after the call.
[07:45] Tom: Networking specifics — if we do Private, we need VPC peering and control-plane egress minimized. Can your Private deployment work in an air-gapped setup?
[07:58] Marco: We do an on-prem package for air-gapped customers; it requires a deployment plan with our infra team. For less stringent needs, VPC-only Private is common.
[08:20] Alyssa: Back to latency — you mentioned quantization and kernel selection. If we use int8 quantized weights for the reranker model, how much latency improvement?
[08:34] Marco: It depends on model/seq lengths, but int8/4-bit paths can yield 1.5–3x throughput improvements. However, quantization can sometimes change output ranking slightly — that's where our evaluation harness helps quantify the change on your dataset.
[09:00] Samir: Competitors like Pinecone tout managed vector DB performance; what's Redwood's advantage here?
[09:12] Jenna: Pinecone focuses on the index; Redwood is the inference runtime + orchestration. If you want a unified Rerank + Embed flow with predictable latency and model rollouts, Redwood gives you the serving runtime, metrics, and rollouts plus integrations to push vectors to Pinecone or host them.
[09:40] Tom: Any recommendations on embedding size if we want to save storage but keep quality?
[09:48] Marco: Start with a short eval: take a representative sample, run 1536 vs 768 embeddings, compare recall/MRR. Sometimes projection or PCA works, or training a smaller model. We can run that as part of a pilot and report tradeoffs.
[10:15] Alyssa: For the reranker, do you recommend cross-encoder vs bi-encoder? We're doing cross-encoder now but it's costly.
[10:25] Marco: A common pattern: use a bi-encoder for retrieval at scale (cheap), then cross-encoder for rerank on a small candidate set. Another approach is an efficient cross-encoder distillation. Redwood supports both and can operate hybrid pipelines.
[11:00] Samir: On the pilot — what would you need from us?
[11:08] Jenna: Ideally: sample dataset (queries + corpus), current embedding model details and dimensionality, expected QPS and latency SLOs, and a short list of success metrics (MRR lift, latency, cost per query).
[11:28] Alyssa: We can deliver that; timeline-wise we'd like a pilot within two weeks. Is that realistic?
[11:35] Marco: Yes, for a 2-week pilot we usually do an initial bench on a subset, then a 2-week production-ish run. Benchmarks require us to spin up GPU nodes if Dedicated or test on Hosted with throttled QPS.
[12:00] Tom: How do you instrument cost? We need token-level or call-level cost breakdowns.
[12:12] Jenna: Redwood Console shows per-route/model token and latency breakdowns, plus trace hooks. We'll share screenshots in the deck; Marco can include what metric exports you'll get.
[12:35] Marco: Also we recommend setting up guardrails — rate limits, fallback policies, and automatic degrade to cheaper model variants if overloaded.
[13:05] Samir: Any gotchas around indexing vectors at scale? We have ~200M vectors now.
[13:16] Marco: For 200M vectors, index choice matters — approximate nearest neighbor index types (HNSW, IVF) and vector compression/quantization. Storage and query latency tradeoffs are real. If you host the index, we provide guidance on sharding and replica count; if you use managed Pinecone, they handle that but you lose some kernel-level tuning.
[13:50] Alyssa: We use HNSW for now.
[13:54] Marco: HNSW is common. For rerank flows you want fast retrieval to keep candidate latency low.
[14:10] Jenna: Quick note on security docs — we'll include SOC 2 cert, pen test summary, and network diagrams.
[14:20] Samir: Good. On pricing — ballpark for Dedicated vs Hosted?
[14:28] Jenna: Hosted is usage-based per token/embedding. Dedicated is reserved capacity (monthly), usually better for large, steady throughput — lower unit cost. Private includes platform fee + support license. We'll send a tailored pricing sheet for your 800 QPS profile.
[15:00] Tom: For Dedicated, what's typical commitment and flexibility?
[15:10] Jenna: Monthly or annual commits. We have burst policies for short spikes and autoscaling configs.
[15:30] Alyssa: One more thing — do you support hybrid search natively (BM25 + vector) or do we handle the orchestration?
[15:40] Marco: Redwood supports hybrid patterns; you can orchestrate in your app or use our per-route pipelines that run a BM25 pass in your search backend and then call Redwood for embedding/rerank. We also provide connectors for OpenSearch to fetch BM25 candidates and then do rerank in Redwood.
[16:05] Samir: Any recommended rerank model families?
[16:12] Marco: For rerank cross-encoders people use mid-sized models (e.g., 3B-ish) for quality/latency tradeoff. Distilled or quantized variants often hit the sweet spot. We'll propose specific families in the pilot plan.
[16:40] Jenna: Alright let's summarize decisions and next steps.
[16:50] Marco: Action recap — Marco will own benchmarks; Jenna will send pricing + security docs; Nimbus will share sample dataset and QPS targets. We'll schedule a bench kickoff.
[17:05] Samir: Yep that's correct. Also curious whether you can run a small bench in our VPC if we opt for Private later.
[17:12] Marco: Yes, we can coordinate with infra teams; Private bench requires some setup but possible.
[17:25] Tom: One nit — we use a custom scoring function on top of embeddings. Can that live as a step inside Redwood?
[17:33] Marco: You can bring custom scoring as a lightweight function (we support function/tool calling / structured output). For Private it can be deployed closer to the data for performance.
[18:00] Alyssa: Okay great, I'll start assembling the dataset and share details by Thursday.
[18:06] Jenna: Thanks everyone. We'll send the deck, pricing, and security docs and propose times for the benchmark kickoff.
[18:18] Samir: Thanks, talk soon.
[40:00] [call disconnected, recording stopped]

Notes: transcription contains a few minor mis-transcriptions (product names, KV cache spoken as "K V cache" in places). There were short cross-talk instances around 05:20 and 11:28.

End of transcript.
